name: Ndolé (Bitterleaf & Peanut Stew)
steps: Boil and aggressively wash the bitterleaf multiple times to remove excess bitterness, then squeeze dry.
Boil the beef or smoked fish until tender, keeping the stock.
Blend the raw peanuts, half an onion, garlic, and ginger with a little water into a smooth paste.
Add the peanut paste to the meat stock and cook for 15 minutes until it thickens.
Stir in the washed bitterleaf, ground crayfish, and shrimp. Simmer for 10 minutes.
In a separate pan, heat the palm oil and fry the remaining sliced onions. Pour this over the stew and turn off the heat.

name: Poulet DG (Chicken & Plantain Skillet)
steps: Peel the ripe plantains, slice them into rounds, and fry until golden brown. Set aside.
Season the chicken with garlic and ginger, then pan-fry or roast until browned and cooked through.
In a large pot, sauté chopped onions, garlic, and tomatoes until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add the chopped carrots, bell peppers, and green beans. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender.
Toss the cooked chicken and fried plantains into the vegetable sauce. Mix gently and simmer for 5 minutes.

name: Eru (Waterleaf & Okok Stew)
steps: Boil the beef skin (Canda) and smoked fish in a pot with a little water and salt until very tender.
Add the chopped waterleaf to the pot. Do not add extra water, as the waterleaf will release its own liquid.
Once the waterleaf has wilted down, add the finely shredded Eru leaves and mix thoroughly.
Stir in the ground crayfish and scotch bonnet pepper.
Pour the palm oil over the mixture. Simmer on low heat until the water evaporates and the oil separates.

name: Koki (Steamed Black-Eyed Pea Pudding)
steps: Soak the black-eyed peas in water for a few hours, then rub them together to remove the skins.
Blend the peeled beans with a little water and the habanero pepper until you get a smooth, thick paste.
Warm the palm oil just until it becomes liquid (do not bleach or overheat it).
Pour the palm oil into the bean paste and mix vigorously in one direction to incorporate air and make it fluffy.
Fold the banana leaves to create pouches, fill them with the mixture, tie them securely, and steam in a pot for 1 to 1.5 hours.
